questions.source: Gate — z vs t decision tree
questions.prompt: Which row of the test-statistic decision tree is CORRECT?
options: σ known → z · σ unknown → t (df = n−1) · testing σ/σ² itself → χ² (df = n−1)
σ known → t · σ unknown → z · σ → F
questions.explain: The opening decision of every exam Q1: **σ known → z; σ unknown → t (df = n−1); claims about spread (σ or σ²) → χ² with χ²₀ = (n−1)s²/σ₀²**.

questions.prompt: x̄ = 4.8 min, σ = 1.2 (known), n = 40, 90% confidence (z = 1.645). Compute the margin of error E (3 decimals).
The CORRECT interpretation of a 95% CI (34.293, 35.290) for mean battery life is:
options: "We are 95% confident the true mean battery life is between 34.293 and 35.290 hours"
"95% of batteries last between 34.293 and 35.290 hours"
"The sample mean has a 95% chance of being in this interval"
questions.explain: The CI speaks about the **true population MEAN**, not individual batteries (that's a prediction interval) nor the sample mean (which is certainly in its own interval). The exact sentence earns the interpretation mark.

questions.prompt: σ = 2.0, desired E = 0.5, 95% (z = 1.96). Required n = ? (whole number)
Claim: "the average is NO MORE than 50" (i.e. μ ≤ 50). The hypotheses are:
options: H₀: μ = 50 (claim side, has equality) vs H₁: μ > 50 — right-tailed; rejecting H₀ rejects the claim
questions.explain: Equality ALWAYS sits in H₀. 'No more than' (≤) contains equality → the claim lives in H₀; H₁ is the complement (μ > 50). Compare: 'exceeds' (>) has no equality → that claim goes to H₁.

questions.prompt: x̄ = 14.15, μ₀ = 15, s = 1.184, n = 10. Compute t₀ (3 decimals, sign matters).
Testing H₁: σ < 2.5 at α = 0.05 with df = 19 — which critical value do you look up?
options: χ²(0.95, 19) = 10.117 — the LEFT tail uses the 0.95 right-tail column; reject if χ²₀ < 10.117
questions.explain: χ² tables list RIGHT-tail areas. A left-tailed test at α = 0.05 needs the value with **0.95 to its right** → χ²(0.95, 19) = 10.117; rejection region is BELOW it. This lookup is the most-lost mark in Q1.

questions.prompt: The full-marks structure for ANY hypothesis test answer is:
options: Hypotheses → test choice (z/t/χ²) → statistic computed → critical value/region → compare → decision (reject / fail to reject) → conclusion sentence with α and context
questions.explain: Markers tick each step: **H₀/H₁ · test selection with reason · computation · critical value · comparison · decision · plain-English conclusion** ('At α = 0.05 there is sufficient/insufficient evidence that…'). Skipping the sentence loses easy marks every time.
